newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX ends bourse trade at lower levels.
newsitem.headline: German DAX ends bourse trade at lower levels.

text.p: Germany's DAX index of 30 German blue-chips ended 1.55 percent lower on Thursday, dragged lower by falling equity futures market and weak sentiment emerging from the U.S.
The DAX index ended at 3,264.67 points, down 51.26 points, while March DAX futures, due to expire on Friday, fell 41.5 points to 3,267.5, exerting a negative effect on the cash market.
Dealers also blamed lower U.S. Treasuries and a fall in the Dow U.S. share index overnight for the weakness. "All in all, there is a lot of pressure on the market today," one said.
Dealers said there was enough potential for uncertainty later on to keep investors sidelined.
U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan is due later to testify before the Joint Economic Committee, while U.S. trade data could have an impact on the dollar, currently trading at 1.67 marks.
The main market focus was the restart of trade in Thyssen and Krupp-Hoesch after two days of suspension related to Krupp's attempt to produce a merger of their steel businesses.
Thyssen ended the session up 29 marks, or 8.36 percent, to 375.80 marks while Krupp shares gained 15.07 percent to 313 marks.
Drugs group Schering climbed 5.75 marks, 3.5 percent, to 162 marks on continued positive reaction to its move on Wednesday to raise its forecast for 1997 results.
A number of stocks suffered profit-taking after recent strong runs.
Software group SAP was down 7.50 marks to 264.80, while a number of shares in the financial sector were lower. Dresdner lost 1.55 marks to end at 54.10.
